long_biography.plain_text:
Italian textile entrepreneur Pier Luigi Loro Piana spent a decade persuading Chinese herders to separate the exceptionally fine undercoat of young goats from adult cashmere. His company’s Italian technicians developed ways to spin and weave the delicate fibre, creating Baby Cashmere for knitwear, fabrics and outerwear.

His search for finer wool also involved rewarding breeders in Australia and New Zealand. Loro Piana’s record-bale competition encouraged improvements in fibre quality; the company kept each winning bale until it acquired an even finer one, then released the previous record into production. Beyond textiles, he competes in maxi sailing and serves as a vice-president of the International Maxi Association.
long_biography.html:
Italian textile entrepreneur Pier Luigi Loro Piana spent a decade persuading Chinese herders to separate the exceptionally fine undercoat of young goats from adult cashmere. His company’s Italian technicians developed ways to spin and weave the delicate fibre, creating Baby Cashmere for knitwear, fabrics and outerwear.

His search for finer wool also involved rewarding breeders in Australia and New Zealand. Loro Piana’s record-bale competition encouraged improvements in fibre quality; the company kept each winning bale until it acquired an even finer one, then released the previous record into production. Beyond textiles, he competes in maxi sailing and serves as a vice-president of the International Maxi Association.
